---- MODULE W4Od15m0p4t5 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction fills a bounded position book using optimistic locking with
\* retry. A trader reads the book's current version, then commits an added position only if the
\* version is unchanged and the book still has room under its capacity bound; a successful commit
\* bumps the version. If the version has moved on, the trader retries by re-reading. A privileged
\* admin may evict a filled position. The number of filled positions never exceeds the bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Slots == {0, 1, 2}
Traders == {0, 1}
Cap == 2
MaxV == 3

VARIABLES book, version, pend, clock

vars == <<book, version, pend, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in SUBSET Slots
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxV
    /\ pend \in [Traders -> [rv : 0 .. MaxV, slot : Slots, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ book = {}
    /\ version = 0
    /\ pend = [t \in Traders |-> [rv |-> 0, slot |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* Optimistically read the version and stage a position to add.
Read(t, s) ==
    /\ ~pend[t].on
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [rv |-> version, slot |-> s, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, version, clock>>

\* Commit only if the version is unchanged and the book has room under the bound.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ pend[t].on
    /\ pend[t].rv = version
    /\ version < MaxV
    /\ pend[t].slot \notin book
    /\ Cardinality(book) < Cap
    /\ book' = book \cup {pend[t].slot}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [rv |-> 0, slot |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The version moved on: retry by re-reading, keeping the intended slot.
Retry(t) ==
    /\ pend[t].on
    /\ pend[t].rv # version
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![t] = [rv |-> version, slot |-> pend[t].slot, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, version, clock>>

\* Admin: evict a filled position from the book.
Evict(s) ==
    /\ s \in book
    /\ book' = book \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pend, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, version, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders, s \in Slots : Read(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Commit(t) \/ Retry(t)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Evict(s)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the number of filled positions never exceeds the bound.
WithinBookCap == Cardinality(book) <= Cap
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction fills a bounded position book using optimistic locking with
retry. A trader first reads the book's current version number and stages a position it wants to
add. It commits the addition only if the version is still unchanged and the book still has room
below its capacity bound; a successful commit inserts the position and bumps the version. If the
version has moved on since the read, the trader retries by re-reading the current version while
keeping the position it intended to add. A privileged admin may evict a filled position from the
book at any time. A housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: optimistically read the version and stage a position to add; commit the staged position
when the version is unchanged and the book has room, bumping the version; retry by re-reading
when the version has moved on; admin-evict a filled position; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of filled positions in the book never exceeds the capacity bound.

---- MODULE W4Od16m1p3t2 ----
\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs two instances that share one pool of dispensing bins,
\* with exclusive access governed by a ring token passed between the instances. Only the token
\* holder may allocate a free bin to a waiting prescription; allocation removes the bin from the
\* free pool and records its owner. Releasing a bin returns it to the free pool and clears its
\* owner. A bin is thus assigned to a prescription exactly when it is not in the free pool, so the
\* same bin is never handed to two prescriptions.
EXTENDS Naturals

Slots == {0, 1, 2}
Rx == {0, 1}
Inst == {"A", "B"}
NONE == 9

VARIABLES token, free, owner, pending

vars == <<token, free, owner, pending>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Inst
    /\ free \in SUBSET Slots
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Rx \cup {NONE}]
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Rx

Init ==
    /\ token = "A"
    /\ free = Slots
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ pending = {}

\* Pass the ring token to the other instance; always available.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = IF token = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, owner, pending>>

\* A prescription arrives and waits for a bin.
Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, free, owner>>

\* The token holder allocates a free bin to a waiting prescription, taking it out of the pool.
Allocate(s, r, i) ==
    /\ token = i
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ s \in free
    /\ owner[s] = NONE
    /\ free' = free \ {s}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* Release a bin, returning it to the free pool and clearing its owner.
Release(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # NONE
    /\ free' = free \cup {s}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Submit(r)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, r \in Rx, i \in Inst : Allocate(s, r, i)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a bin is owned exactly when it is not in the free pool, so a bin can
\* never be handed out while it is still advertised as free (and thus grabbed twice).
FreeCoherent == \A s \in Slots : (owner[s] # NONE) <=> (s \notin free)
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs two independent instances that share one pool of
dispensing bins, with exclusive access to the pool governed by a ring token passed back and forth
between the two instances. A prescription arrives and waits for a bin. Only the instance currently
holding the ring token may allocate a free bin to a waiting prescription; allocating removes the
bin from the free pool and records the prescription as its owner. Releasing a bin returns it to
the free pool and clears its owner. Because a bin is recorded as owned exactly when it has been
taken out of the free pool, a bin can never be handed to a second prescription while it is still
advertised as free.

Actions: pass the ring token to the other instance; submit a prescription that waits for a bin;
the token holder allocates a free bin to a waiting prescription, removing it from the pool;
release a bin, returning it to the free pool and clearing its owner.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every bin is owned by a prescription exactly when it is not in the free pool, so
the same bin is never allocated to two prescriptions at once.

---- MODULE W4Od15m1p1t0 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction lets only the trader holding the ring token touch the shared
\* fill counter. A holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add against that reading, then
\* writes it back absolutely -- but passing the token discards any stage the leaving holder still
\* had, so a write always reflects the reading taken during the current, uninterrupted hold. One
\* trader may crash silently. The shared counter always equals the sum of each trader's own
\* contributions, so no committed add is ever lost by a stale write.
EXTENDS Naturals

Traders == {0, 1, 2}
N == 3
MaxTotal == 2

VARIABLES token, total, contrib, crashed, staged

vars == <<token, total, contrib, crashed, staged>>

Sum == contrib[0] + contrib[1] + contrib[2]

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Traders
    /\ total \in 0 .. MaxTotal
    /\ contrib \in [Traders -> 0 .. MaxTotal]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Traders
    /\ staged \in [Traders -> [base : 0 .. MaxTotal, on : BOOLEAN]]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ total = 0
    /\ contrib = [t \in Traders |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ staged = [t \in Traders |-> [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]

\* Pass the ring token onward, discarding the leaving holder's staged write.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % N
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![token] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<total, contrib, crashed>>

\* The token holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add against that reading.
Read(t) ==
    /\ t = token
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ ~staged[t].on
    /\ total < MaxTotal
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> total, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, total, contrib, crashed>>

\* The holder writes its staged add back absolutely and records its own contribution.
Write(t) ==
    /\ t = token
    /\ staged[t].on
    /\ total' = staged[t].base + 1
    /\ contrib' = [contrib EXCEPT ![t] = contrib[t] + 1]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed>>

\* One trader may crash silently, dropping any staged write.
Crash(t) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {t}
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, total, contrib>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Read(t) \/ Write(t) \/ Crash(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the shared counter equals the sum of every trader's own contributions.
NoLostAdd == total = Sum
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction lets only the trader currently holding the ring token touch the
shared fill counter. A holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add computed from that
reading, then writes the new value back absolutely. Passing the ring token onward discards any
staged write the leaving holder still had, so a write always reflects the reading the holder took
during its current, uninterrupted hold of the token. One trader may crash silently, dropping any
staged write it had. Each trader also keeps a tally of its own contributions. Because only the
token holder writes and a stage cannot survive a token pass, no add based on a stale reading can
overwrite the counter, and no committed add is lost.

Actions: pass the ring token onward, discarding the leaving holder's staged write; the token
holder reads the counter and stages a one-lot add; the holder writes its staged add back
absolutely and records its own contribution; one trader crashes silently, dropping its stage.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared fill counter always equals the sum of every trader's own recorded
contributions, so no committed add is ever lost by a stale write.

---- MODULE W4Od12m8p4t1 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker guards its fridges with hierarchical locks: a coarse fridge
\* lock and a fine per-shelf lock. Storing a unit onto a shelf requires holding both the fridge
\* lock and that shelf's lock, and is only allowed while the shelf is below its capacity bound.
\* Store orders arrive in an inbox and may be honoured out of order. Units may also be withdrawn.
\* No shelf ever holds more units than its capacity bound.
EXTENDS Naturals

Shelves == {0, 1}
Workers == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
Cap == 2

VARIABLES fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock

vars == <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridgeLock \in Workers \cup {FREE}
    /\ shelfLock \in [Shelves -> Workers \cup {FREE}]
    /\ stored \in [Shelves -> 0 .. Cap]
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET Shelves
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ fridgeLock = FREE
    /\ shelfLock = [s \in Shelves |-> FREE]
    /\ stored = [s \in Shelves |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* A store order for a shelf arrives in the inbox (may be honoured out of order later).
Request(s) ==
    /\ s \notin inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, clock>>

\* Grab the coarse fridge lock.
GrabFridge(w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = FREE
    /\ fridgeLock' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Grab a shelf's fine lock while holding the fridge lock.
GrabShelf(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = FREE
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Store a unit onto a shelf, holding both locks and below the shelf's capacity bound.
Store(s, w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ s \in inbox
    /\ stored[s] < Cap
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![s] = stored[s] + 1]
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, clock>>

\* Withdraw a unit from a shelf.
Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ stored[s] > 0
    /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![s] = stored[s] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, inbox, clock>>

\* Release a shelf lock.
ReleaseShelf(s, w) ==
    /\ shelfLock[s] = w
    /\ shelfLock' = [shelfLock EXCEPT ![s] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Release the fridge lock once no shelf is still locked by this worker.
ReleaseFridge(w) ==
    /\ fridgeLock = w
    /\ \A s \in Shelves : shelfLock[s] # w
    /\ fridgeLock' = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfLock, stored, inbox, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, shelfLock, stored, inbox>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Shelves : Request(s) \/ Withdraw(s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : GrabFridge(w) \/ ReleaseFridge(w)
    \/ \E s \in Shelves, w \in Workers : GrabShelf(s, w) \/ Store(s, w) \/ ReleaseShelf(s, w)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: no shelf ever holds more units than its capacity bound.
WithinShelfCap == \A s \in Shelves : stored[s] <= Cap
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards its fridges with two levels of hierarchical locks: a coarse
lock over a fridge and a fine lock over each shelf. To store a unit onto a shelf, a worker must
hold both the fridge lock and that shelf's lock, and the store is allowed only while the shelf is
below its capacity bound. Store orders arrive in an inbox and may be honoured out of order, so the
order in which shelves are stocked need not match the order the orders came in. Units may also be
withdrawn from a shelf. A worker cannot release a fridge lock while it still holds any shelf lock
inside that fridge. A housekeeping pulse ticks throughout.

Actions: a store order for a shelf arrives in the inbox; grab the coarse fridge lock; grab a
shelf's fine lock while holding the fridge lock; store a unit onto a shelf while holding both locks
and below capacity, consuming its order; withdraw a unit from a shelf; release a shelf lock;
release the fridge lock once no shelf is still locked by the worker; tick the housekeeping pulse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no shelf ever holds more units than its capacity bound.

---- MODULE W4Od15m3p2t4 ----
\* A stock-exchange opening auction, coordinated by an elected leader (with failover to a new
\* term), keeps a fixed quantity of shares distributed across three books: available, locked, and
\* executed. The leader locks available shares for matching -- bounded by a runtime-adjustable
\* capacity -- executes locked shares, or unlocks them back to available. Shares are conserved:
\* the three books always sum to the fixed total, no share created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals

Total == 3
MaxTerm == 1
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES avail, locked, executed, capacity, term

vars == <<avail, locked, executed, capacity, term>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ avail \in 0 .. Total
    /\ locked \in 0 .. Total
    /\ executed \in 0 .. Total
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm

Init ==
    /\ avail = Total
    /\ locked = 0
    /\ executed = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ term = 0

\* Failover: elect a fresh leader term, cycling within a bounded band.
Elect ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, locked, executed, capacity>>

\* Lock available shares for matching, staying within the current capacity.
Lock(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= avail
    /\ locked + k <= capacity
    /\ avail' = avail - k
    /\ locked' = locked + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<executed, capacity, term>>

\* Execute locked shares, moving them to the executed book.
Execute(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= locked
    /\ locked' = locked - k
    /\ executed' = executed + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, capacity, term>>

\* Unlock shares back to the available book.
Unlock(k) ==
    /\ k > 0
    /\ k <= locked
    /\ locked' = locked - k
    /\ avail' = avail + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<executed, capacity, term>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime to a different value; always available.
Resize(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, locked, executed, term>>

Next ==
    \/ Elect
    \/ \E k \in 1 .. Total : Lock(k) \/ Execute(k) \/ Unlock(k)
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: available, locked, and executed shares always sum to the fixed total.
SharesConserved == avail + locked + executed = Total
====
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction is coordinated by an elected leader that fails over to a fresh
term when needed. It keeps a fixed quantity of shares distributed across three books: available,
locked, and executed. The leader locks available shares for matching, but only so far as the
locked total stays within a capacity that can be adjusted at runtime. Locked shares may then be
executed, moving them into the executed book, or unlocked, moving them back to available. The
capacity may be resized at runtime to a different value. No share is ever created or destroyed.

Actions: fail over by electing a fresh leader term; lock available shares for matching while
within capacity; execute locked shares into the executed book; unlock locked shares back to
available; resize the matching capacity at runtime.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the available, locked, and executed share counts always sum to the fixed total,
so no share is ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od13m1p1t5 ----
\* A vending-machine network shares one mechanical vend meter, writable only by the machine
\* holding the ring token. A holder reads the meter and later writes it back as the read value
\* plus one, logging the vend. Passing the token discards any read the leaving holder still had,
\* so a write reflects the meter as read during the current, uninterrupted hold. A privileged
\* admin may override, clearing all outstanding reads. The meter always equals the number of
\* vends recorded in the log, so no vend is lost by a stale write.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Machines == {0, 1}
N == 2
MaxVends == 3

VARIABLES token, meter, vendLog, staged

vars == <<token, meter, vendLog, staged>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Machines
    /\ meter \in 0 .. MaxVends
    /\ vendLog \in Seq(Machines)
    /\ staged \in [Machines -> [rm : 0 .. MaxVends, on : BOOLEAN]]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ meter = 0
    /\ vendLog = <<>>
    /\ staged = [m \in Machines |-> [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]

\* Pass the ring token, discarding the leaving holder's staged read.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % N
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![token] = [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<meter, vendLog>>

\* The token holder reads the current meter value.
Read(m) ==
    /\ m = token
    /\ ~staged[m].on
    /\ meter < MaxVends
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = [rm |-> meter, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, meter, vendLog>>

\* The holder writes the meter back as its read value plus one, logging the vend.
Vend(m) ==
    /\ m = token
    /\ staged[m].on
    /\ Len(vendLog) < MaxVends
    /\ meter' = staged[m].rm + 1
    /\ vendLog' = Append(vendLog, m)
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![m] = [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

\* Admin override: clear all outstanding reads; always available.
Override ==
    /\ staged' = [m \in Machines |-> [rm |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, meter, vendLog>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Read(m) \/ Vend(m)
    \/ Override

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the meter equals the number of vends recorded in the log.
NoLostVend == meter = Len(vendLog)
====
nl:
A vending-machine network shares a single mechanical vend meter, which may be written only by the
machine currently holding the ring token. A holder first reads the current meter value. Later it
writes the meter back as the value it read plus one, and logs the vend. Passing the ring token
onward discards any read the leaving holder still had outstanding, so a write always reflects the
meter value as it was read during the holder's current, uninterrupted hold of the token. A
privileged admin may override at any time, clearing all outstanding reads. Because a stale read
cannot survive a token pass, no vend based on an out-of-date meter reading can overwrite the meter
and lose a vend.

Actions: pass the ring token, discarding the leaving holder's staged read; the token holder reads
the current meter; the holder writes the meter back as its read value plus one and logs the vend;
admin-override to clear all outstanding reads.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the vend meter always equals the number of vends recorded in the log, so no vend
is ever lost by a stale write.

---- MODULE W4Od1m7p2t3 ----
\* An air-traffic runway allocator exposes its free-slot count as a compare-and-swap register.
\* A controller reads the free count, stages an assignment to a runway, and commits only if the
\* free count is still on the value it read; the commit writes the free count absolutely as the
\* read value minus one and adds a slot to that runway. A slow controller whose reading is stale
\* simply retries. Slots are conserved: free slots plus slots assigned across the runways always
\* total the fixed pool.
EXTENDS Naturals

Runways == {0, 1}
Controllers == {0, 1}
Total == 3

VARIABLES free, assigned, attempt, clock

vars == <<free, assigned, attempt, clock>>

Sum == assigned[0] + assigned[1]

TypeOK ==
    /\ free \in 0 .. Total
    /\ assigned \in [Runways -> 0 .. Total]
    /\ attempt \in [Controllers -> [exp : 0 .. Total, rw : Runways, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ free = Total
    /\ assigned = [r \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ attempt = [c \in Controllers |-> [exp |-> 0, rw |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ clock = 0

\* A controller reads the free count and stages an assignment to a runway.
Read(c, r) ==
    /\ ~attempt[c].on
    /\ free > 0
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> free, rw |-> r, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, assigned, clock>>

\* Commit only if the free count is still on the read value; write it absolutely, assign a slot.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ attempt[c].on
    /\ attempt[c].exp = free
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = attempt[c].exp - 1
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![attempt[c].rw] = assigned[attempt[c].rw] + 1]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> 0, rw |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* A slow controller whose reading is stale retries by re-reading, keeping its target runway.
Retry(c) ==
    /\ attempt[c].on
    /\ attempt[c].exp # free
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> free, rw |-> attempt[c].rw, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, assigned, clock>>

\* Release a slot from a runway back to the free pool.
Release(r) ==
    /\ assigned[r] > 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = assigned[r] - 1]
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempt, clock>>

\* Timing pulse standing in for the passage of time; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, assigned, attempt>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : Read(c, r)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Commit(c) \/ Retry(c)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Release(r)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: free slots plus slots assigned across all runways always total the pool.
SlotsConserved == free + Sum = Total
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator exposes its count of free departure slots as a single
compare-and-swap register. A controller first reads the free-slot count and stages an assignment
of a slot to a particular runway, remembering the count it read. It commits the assignment only
if the free count is still sitting on exactly the value it read; the commit then writes the free
count back absolutely as that read value minus one and adds a slot to the chosen runway. A slow
controller whose reading has gone stale -- because the free count moved on before it committed --
simply retries by re-reading, keeping the runway it intended. A slot assigned to a runway may be
released back to the free pool. Slots are neither created nor destroyed.

Actions: read the free count and stage a runway assignment; commit an assignment when the free
count still matches the reading, writing the count absolutely and assigning a slot; retry by
re-reading when the reading is stale; release a slot from a runway to the free pool; tick the clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the free slots plus the slots assigned across all runways always total the fixed
pool, so no slot is ever created or destroyed by a stale write.

---- MODULE W4Od19m8p4t4 ----
\* A library book-reservation system guards reservations with hierarchical locks: a coarse catalog
\* lock and a fine per-copy lock. A member reserves a copy only while holding both the catalog lock
\* and that copy's lock, and only while the total number of reservations is below a capacity bound.
\* The capacity may be adjusted at runtime, but never below the number of copies already reserved.
\* The total number of reserved copies never exceeds the capacity bound.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Copies == {0, 1, 2}
Members == {0, 1}
FREE == 9
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES catalogLock, copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock

vars == <<catalogLock, copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ catalogLock \in Members \cup {FREE}
    /\ copyLock \in [Copies -> Members \cup {FREE}]
    /\ reserved \in SUBSET Copies
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ catalogLock = FREE
    /\ copyLock = [c \in Copies |-> FREE]
    /\ reserved = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ clock = 0

\* Grab the coarse catalog lock.
GrabCatalog(m) ==
    /\ catalogLock = FREE
    /\ catalogLock' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copyLock, reserved, capacity, clock>>

\* Grab a copy's fine lock while holding the catalog lock.
GrabCopy(c, m) ==
    /\ catalogLock = m
    /\ copyLock[c] = FREE

\* nominated, others vote, and a strict majority elects a unique winner for that seat. Only that
\* winner may be allocated the seat, and only while the total seats allocated stays under a
\* runtime-adjustable capacity. Because a seat is only ever held by its quorum-elected winner, the
\* same seat is never allocated to two different players.

Seats == {0, 1}
Players == {0, 1, 2}
NONE == 9
MaxCap == 2

vars == <<nominee, votes, winner, owner, capacity>>

Owned == Cardinality({s \in Seats : owner[s] # NONE})

    /\ nominee \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ votes \in [Seats -> SUBSET Players]
    /\ winner \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ owner \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap

    /\ nominee = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ votes = [s \in Seats |-> {}]
    /\ winner = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ owner = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

Nominate(s, p) ==
    /\ nominee[s] = NONE
    /\ winner[s] = NONE
    /\ owner[s] = NONE

    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]

    /\ nominee' = [nominee EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]

\* stages: pending, queued, processing, and dispensed. Enqueuing applies backpressure -- a pending
\* prescription joins the bounded work queue only while the queue is below its capacity, and that
\* capacity may change at runtime. Prescriptions then move to processing and finally to dispensed.
\* No prescription is created or destroyed: the four stages always sum to the fixed total.

Total == 3
MaxCap == 3

vars == <<pending, queued, processing, dispensed, capacity>>

    /\ pending \in 0 .. Total

    /\ processing \in 0 .. Total
    /\ dispensed \in 0 .. Total

    /\ queued = 0
    /\ processing = 0
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

    /\ queued < capacity
    /\ pending' = pending - 1
    /\ queued' = queued + 1

\* Pull a queued prescription into processing.

    /\ queued > 0
    /\ queued' = queued - 1
    /\ processing' = processing + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, dispensed, capacity>>

    /\ processing' = processing - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1

\* Return a dispensed prescription to pending (e.g. a refill cycle).

    /\ dispensed > 0
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1
    /\ pending' = pending + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, processing, capacity>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queued, processing, dispensed>>

    \/ Dispense
    \/ Recycle
    \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(c)

RxConserved == pending + queued + processing + dispensed = Total

---- MODULE W4Od12m2p1t0 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker updates its shared stock through two-phase commit. Preparing a
\* transaction acquires the single write lock and reads the current stock as the transaction's
\* base; committing writes the stock back absolutely as that base plus one and logs the unit.
\* Because the write lock serializes preparers, a commit's base is never stale, so no update is
\* lost. One participant may crash silently, releasing any lock it held. The stock always equals
\* the total of the units logged.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

TX == {0, 1}
NONE == 9
MaxStock == 3
MaxLog == 3

VARIABLES stock, writeLock, prep, log, crashed, clock

vars == <<stock, writeLock, prep, log, crashed, clock>>

RECURSIVE Total(_)
Total(s) == IF s = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE Head(s) + Total(Tail(s))

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in 0 .. MaxStock
    /\ writeLock \in TX \cup {NONE}
    /\ prep \in [TX -> [base : 0 .. MaxStock, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ log \in Seq({1})
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET TX
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ stock = 0
    /\ writeLock = NONE
    /\ prep = [t \in TX |-> [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ clock = 0

\* Prepare: acquire the write lock and read the current stock as the base.
Prepare(t) ==
    /\ writeLock = NONE
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ ~prep[t].on
    /\ stock < MaxStock
    /\ writeLock' = t
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> stock, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, log, crashed, clock>>

\* Commit: write the stock back absolutely as base plus one and log the unit; release the lock.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ writeLock = t
    /\ prep[t].on
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ stock' = prep[t].base + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, 1)
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ writeLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, clock>>

\* Abort: release the write lock without committing.
Abort(t) ==
    /\ writeLock = t
    /\ prep[t].on
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ writeLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, log, crashed, clock>>

\* One participant crashes silently, releasing any lock and preparation it held.
Crash(t) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {t}
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![t] = [base |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ writeLock' = IF writeLock = t THEN NONE ELSE writeLock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, log, clock>>

\* Housekeeping pulse; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, writeLock, prep, log, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in TX : Prepare(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Abort(t) \/ Crash(t)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: the shared stock equals the total of every unit recorded in the log.
NoLostUnit == stock = Total(log)
====

---- MODULE W4Od2m9p0t3 ----
\* A warehouse robot fleet coordinates exclusive access to a critical charging zone with a single
\* physical key, reissued each epoch. A robot requests the zone, takes the key while it is free,
\* and enters the zone only while holding the key. A robot may be slow to leave -- nothing forces
\* it out -- but it is never failed. Reconfiguring to a new epoch clears the key, the occupant, and
\* all requests. Whoever is inside the zone holds the key, so two robots are never inside at once.
EXTENDS Naturals

Robots == {0, 1, 2}
NONE == 9
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, key, owner, requests

vars == <<epoch, key, owner, requests>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ key \in Robots \cup {NONE}
    /\ owner \in Robots \cup {NONE}
    /\ requests \in SUBSET Robots

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ key = NONE
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ requests = {}

\* Reconfigure to the next epoch, clearing the key, the occupant, and all requests.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % (MaxEpoch + 1)
    /\ key' = NONE
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ requests' = {}

\* A robot requests the critical zone.
Request(r) ==
    /\ r \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, owner>>

\* A requesting robot takes the key while it is free.
TakeKey(r) ==
    /\ key = NONE
    /\ r \in requests
    /\ key' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, requests>>

\* A robot enters the zone only while it holds the key.
Enter(r) ==
    /\ key = r
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ owner' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, requests>>

\* The occupant leaves the zone (it may be slow to do so, but is never failed).
Exit(r) ==
    /\ owner = r
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, key, requests>>

\* A robot not inside the zone drops the key, clearing its request.
DropKey(r) ==
    /\ key = r
    /\ owner # r
    /\ key' = NONE
    /\ requests' = requests \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Request(r) \/ TakeKey(r) \/ Enter(r) \/ Exit(r) \/ DropKey(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: whoever is inside the critical zone holds the single key, so two robots can
\* never be inside the zone at the same time.
MutexByKey == owner # NONE => key = owner

a requesting robot may take it, and a robot may enter the zone only while it is holding the key. A

SAFETY PROPERTY: whoever is inside the critical charging zone is holding the single key, so two
robots are never inside the zone at the same time.

a car; a granted car posts an enter request into the inbox; honour an enter request from the current
grantee while the tunnel is free; the tunnel car exits, releasing the grant; drop a stale request
from a non-grantee car.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whoever is in the wash tunnel is the currently granted car, so two cars are never
in the tunnel at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m3p5t5 ----
\* A smart-home door-lock network can irreversibly burn a lock's master key, coordinated by an
\* elected leader (with failover on a fresh term). Each key lives in exactly one of three disjoint
\* states: intact, pending (staged for burning), or burned. The leader stages an intact key, then
\* irreversibly burns a pending key into the terminal burned state. A privileged admin may override a
\* pending key back to intact. Because the states stay disjoint and burning requires the key to be
\* pending, a key is burned at most once.
EXTENDS Naturals

Keys == {0, 1}
Coords == {0, 1}
MaxTerm == 1

VARIABLES term, leader, intact, pending, burned

vars == <<term, leader, intact, pending, burned>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Coords
    /\ intact \in SUBSET Keys
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Keys
    /\ burned \in SUBSET Keys

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = 0
    /\ intact = Keys
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ burned = {}

\* Failover: elect a fresh leader on the next term.
Elect(k) ==
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % (MaxTerm + 1)
    /\ leader' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<intact, pending, burned>>

\* The leader stages an intact key for burning.
Stage(key) ==
    /\ key \in intact
    /\ intact' = intact \ {key}
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {key}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, burned>>

\* Irreversibly burn a pending key into the terminal burned state.
Burn(key) ==
    /\ key \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {key}
    /\ burned' = burned \cup {key}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, intact>>

\* Admin override: return a pending key to intact.
Override(key) ==
    /\ key \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {key}
    /\ intact' = intact \cup {key}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, burned>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Coords : Elect(k)
    \/ \E key \in Keys : Stage(key) \/ Burn(key) \/ Override(key)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: the intact, pending, and burned states are pairwise disjoint, so a burned key is in
\* no other state and can never be staged and burned again.
KeyStatesDisjoint ==
    /\ intact \cap pending = {}
    /\ pending \cap burned = {}
    /\ intact \cap burned = {}
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network can irreversibly burn a lock's master key, coordinated by an elected
leader that fails over to a fresh term when needed. Each key is always in exactly one of three
disjoint states: intact, pending (staged for burning), or burned. The leader stages an intact key,
moving it to pending. Burning a pending key is the irreversible act: it moves the key into the
terminal burned state. A privileged admin may override a pending key back to intact. Because the
three states are kept disjoint and burning requires the key to be pending, a key can be burned at
most once.

Actions: fail over by electing a fresh leader on the next term; the leader stages an intact key into
pending; irreversibly burn a pending key into the terminal burned state; admin-override a pending key
back to intact.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the intact, pending, and burned states are always pairwise disjoint, so a burned key
is in no other state and its irreversible burn can never happen a second time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m5p6t2 ----
\* An airport baggage router runs two instances that share one pool of routing decisions. Either
\* instance proposes a decision; voters approve it, and a decision reaches "approved" only with a
\* strict-majority quorum. A decision may be enacted on the belts only once it is approved. Thus no
\* decision is ever enacted by an unauthorized route lacking quorum: the enacted decisions are always
\* a subset of the approved ones.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Decisions == {0, 1}
Voters == {0, 1, 2}
Inst == {"A", "B"}

VARIABLES proposed, approved, votes, applied, turn

vars == <<proposed, approved, votes, applied, turn>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ proposed \in SUBSET Decisions
    /\ approved \in SUBSET Decisions
    /\ votes \in [Decisions -> SUBSET Voters]
    /\ applied \in SUBSET Decisions
    /\ turn \in Inst

Init ==
    /\ proposed = {}
    /\ approved = {}
    /\ votes = [d \in Decisions |-> {}]
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ turn = "A"

\* Either instance proposes a fresh routing decision into the shared pool.
Propose(i, d) ==
    /\ d \notin proposed
    /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {d}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approved, applied, turn>>

\* A voter approves a proposed decision.
Vote(d, v) ==
    /\ d \in proposed
    /\ v \notin votes[d]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = votes[d] \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, approved, applied, turn>>

\* A decision reaching a strict-majority quorum becomes approved.
Approve(d) ==
    /\ d \in proposed
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes[d]) > Cardinality(Voters)
    /\ approved' = approved \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, applied, turn>>

\* Enact an approved decision on the belts.
Apply(d) ==
    /\ d \in approved
    /\ d \notin applied
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, approved, votes, turn>>

\* The two instances take turns polling the shared decision pool; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ turn' = IF turn = "A" THEN "B" ELSE "A"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, approved, votes, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Inst, d \in Decisions : Propose(i, d)
    \/ \E d \in Decisions, v \in Voters : Vote(d, v)
    \/ \E d \in Decisions : Approve(d) \/ Apply(d)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized action: every enacted decision is one that was approved by quorum, so no route is
\* ever enacted without authorization.
OnlyApprovedEnacted == applied \subseteq approved
====
nl:
An airport baggage router runs two independent instances that share one pool of routing decisions.
Either instance may propose a fresh routing decision into the shared pool, which resets that
decision's votes. Voters then approve a proposed decision, and a decision becomes approved only once
a strict majority of voters has voted for it. A decision may be enacted on the belts only once it is
approved. The two instances take turns polling the shared decision pool. Because a decision is
enacted only after it has been approved by quorum, no routing decision is ever enacted by an
unauthorized route that lacks quorum backing.

Actions: either instance proposes a routing decision into the shared pool; a voter approves a
proposed decision; a decision reaching a strict-majority quorum becomes approved; enact an approved
decision on the belts; alternate the polling turn between the two instances.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every routing decision enacted on the belts is one that was approved by a quorum, so
no decision is ever enacted without authorization.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m7p4t4 ----
\* A container-ship crane yard tracks its active operations in a shared count exposed as a
\* compare-and-swap register. To start an operation a crane reads the count and commits an increment
\* only if the count is still on the value it read and is below the capacity bound; the commit writes
\* the read value plus one. If the register moved on, the crane retries. Operations finish, lowering
\* the count. The capacity may change at runtime but never below the current count. The active count
\* never exceeds the capacity.
EXTENDS Naturals

Cranes == {0, 1}
MaxCap == 2

VARIABLES active, pend, capacity, clock

vars == <<active, pend, capacity, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ active \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ pend \in [Cranes -> [exp : 0 .. MaxCap, on : BOOLEAN]]
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ clock \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ active = 0
    /\ pend = [c \in Cranes |-> [exp |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ clock = 0

\* Read the shared active count to start an operation.
Read(c) ==
    /\ ~pend[c].on
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> active, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, capacity, clock>>

\* Commit an increment only if the register is still on the read value and below the bound.
Commit(c) ==
    /\ pend[c].on
    /\ pend[c].exp = active
    /\ active < capacity
    /\ active' = pend[c].exp + 1
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> 0, on |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, clock>>

\* The register moved on: retry by re-reading.
Retry(c) ==
    /\ pend[c].on
    /\ pend[c].exp # active
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![c] = [exp |-> active, on |-> TRUE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, capacity, clock>>

\* An active operation finishes, lowering the count.
Finish ==
    /\ active > 0
    /\ active' = active - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, capacity, clock>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime, but never below the current active count.
Resize(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ k >= active
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, pend, clock>>

\* Yard clock; always available.
Tick ==
    /\ clock' = 1 - clock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, pend, capacity>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Read(c) \/ Commit(c) \/ Retry(c)
    \/ Finish
    \/ \E k \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(k)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity: the active operation count never exceeds the capacity bound.
WithinActiveCap == active <= capacity
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard tracks the number of active operations in a shared count exposed as a
single compare-and-swap register. To start an operation, a crane reads the current active count and
then commits an increment, but only if the register is still sitting on exactly the value it read
and that value is below the capacity bound; the commit writes the read value plus one. If the
register has moved on since the read, the crane retries by re-reading. An active operation later
finishes, lowering the count. The capacity may be changed at runtime to a different value, but is
never lowered below the current active count.

Actions: read the active count to start an operation; commit an increment when the register still
matches the read and is below capacity, writing the read value plus one; retry by re-reading when the
register moved on; finish an active operation, lowering the count; resize the capacity at runtime,
never below the current count; tick the yard clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of active crane operations never exceeds the capacity bound.
